reasoning: This case satisfies the WHO-UMC criteria for 'Certain'. The event followed a plausible temporal sequence after exposure, it resolved on withdrawal, it is a pharmacologically recognised effect of the drug class, and a rechallenge reproduced it within twelve hours in the same anatomical distribution. Crucially, the alternatives are positively excluded rather than merely unmentioned: the patient was taking no other medications and had no significant comorbidity. 'Certain' requires a satisfactory rechallenge, and an inadvertent one occurred here.
major_uncertainty: The rechallenge was inadvertent rather than controlled, and the reported adolescent reaction could not be verified against records. Neither materially weakens the assessment, since the documented dechallenge-rechallenge sequence stands on its own.
